test_cases.desc: storm-action command - port disable, ingress port on stack master
test_cases.method:
1. Device should be configured with 2 vlans on test ports. vlanA (traffic), vlanB(test for connectivity)
2. Enable QoS storm-protection
3. Set storm-rate 700kbps and storm-window to 500 ms
4. Set storm-action to linkdown, storm-downtime to large value - say 60 seconds
5. Set QoS service policy on port
6. Create a scapy packet list of some 1,500,000 bits for transmssion on vlanA.
7. Verify that port is up & clear buffered log
8. Transmit stream at 1,000,000bps 
9. Wait and verify port goes down via log messages
10. Verify that traffic on vlanB is blocked by sending layer 2 packets between test ports.
11. remove service policy / set storm-action to port-disable / add service policy/clear buffered log
    Note: Assuming that removing the service policy will reset the port
12. Transmit stream at 1,000,000bps on vlanA
13. Verify that traffic on vlanB is blocked by sending l2 packets between test ports.
14. Wait for storm-protection to timeout
15. Transmit stream at 1,000,000bps on vlanA in the other direction 
16. Verify that traffic on vlanA is blocked, but vlanB is not blocked, by sending layer 2 packets between test ports.
    Note: check native vlan as well as other trunk mode vlan

Step  8 - Confirm whole stack boots correct software, and reforms withing 20 minutes

Step 10 - Power-off that stack member
Step 11 - Set current software to be the system boot version
Step 12 - Reboot the powered-on stack members
Step 13 - Confirm stack boots correct software, and reforms withing 20 minutes
Step 14 - Power-on the remaining stack member
Step 15 - Confirm whole stack boots correct software, and reforms withing 20 minutes

test_cases.desc: Packets sent out trunk port are correctly double-tagged.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send packets in through customer edge port and out trunk port.
step 2 - Check packets sent out have CID tag and original VID tag.

test_cases.desc: Double-tagged packets sent in the trunk port are stripped and sent to the customer port.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send double-tagged packets through the trunk port and out the customer port.
step 2 - Check packets leaving the customer port have had the CID tag removed.

test_cases.desc: Double-tagged packets sent in the trunk port are dropped if they don't match the ports VLAN/s.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send double-tagged packets with a mis-matching VLAN tag through the trunk port and out the customer port.
step 2 - Check no packets leave the customer port.

test_cases.desc: Packets sent in the trunk port are dropped if they are not tagged.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send un-tagged packets through the trunk port and out the customer port.
step 2 - Check no packets leave the customer port.

test_cases.desc: Trunk port cannot be set as an access/customer-edge port as well.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Attempt to set trunk port to access and customer-edge-port.
step 2 - Check no change in port settings has taken place.

test_cases.desc: Customer-edge-port cannot be set to trunk mode.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Attempt to set customer-edge-port to trunk mode.
step 2 - Check no change in port settings has taken place.

test_cases.desc: Trunk port in multiple VLANs only sends packets to the tagged VLAN.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Create an additional vlan 30 and add portC and trunk port to it.
step 2 - Send in vlan tagged packets for both vlans.
step 3 - Check each customer port recieves only the number of packets that were tagged for it.

test_cases.desc: Trunk port in single VLAN doesn't send packets to VLAN it's not a member of.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Create an additional vlan 30 and add only portC to it.
step 2 - Send in packets with vlan tags for either vlan 20 or 30.
step 3 - Check that the vlan 20 packets are forwarded but the vlan 30 packets are not.

test_cases.desc: Multiple customer edge ports in the same VLAN all receive the same packets.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Add portC as a customer-edge-port in VLAN 20.
step 2 - Send a series of packets through trunk port with different tags.
step 3 - Check both customer-edge-ports receive the same and only those same packets.

test_cases.desc: VLAN hopping attack.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Create an additional vlan 30 and add portC and portB to it.
step 2 - Send in packets from customer-edge-port A with vlan 30 tags.
step 3 - Check that the packets are dropped and not sent to vlan 30.

test_cases.desc: Customer edge port can be a member of only one VLAN.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Create an additional vlan 30.
step 2 - Add portA to the new VLAN, check portA is only a member of one VLAN.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN intra-communication.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send packets from isolated host ports to promiscuous port, expected to arrive.
step 2 - Send packets from isolated host ports to each other, should not arrive.

test_cases.desc: Community VLAN intra-communication.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send packets from host ports to promiscuous port, expected to arrive.
step 2 - Send packets from host ports to each other, expected to arrive.

test_cases.desc: Community VLAN inter-communication.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send packets from community host ports in different vlans to promiscuous port, expected to arrive.
step 2 - Send packets from community host ports in different vlans to each other, should not arrive.

test_cases.desc: Untagged broadcast from promiscuous port goes to all host ports.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set-up an isolated secondary VLAN and a community secondary VLAN.
step 2 - Send un-tagged broadcast packets through the promiscuous port, all host ports should receive them.

test_cases.desc: Tagged broadcasts packets go only to the tagged VLAN.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set-up an isolated secondary VLAN and a community secondary VLAN.
step 2 - Send tagged broadcast packets through the promiscuous port, VLAN matching host port only should receive them.

test_cases.desc: Community VLAN broadcast packets from a host port are received by all other ports.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send broadcast packets through a host port.
step 2 - Confirm packets are received by the other host port and the promiscuous port.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN broadcast packets from a host port only reach the promiscuous port.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send broadcast packets through a host port.
step 2 - Confirm packets are received by only the promiscuous port.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN intra-communication. Host port -> promiscuous port.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send packets from isolated host ports to promiscuous port, expected to arrive.
step 2 - Send packets from isolated host ports to each other, should not arrive.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN intra-communication. Promiscuous port -> host ports.
test_cases.method: step 1 - Send packets from promiscuous port to host ports, expected to arrive.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN host port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send broadcast packets through host ports.
step 2 - Check all are forwarded out the promiscuous port and none out other host ports.

test_cases.desc: Isolated VLAN promiscuous port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Send tagged broadcast packets into the VLAN via the promiscuous port.
step 2 - Check they are forwarded out both host ports.

test_cases.desc: Multiple isolated vlans with same promiscuous port in both, promiscuous port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a second isolated VLAN 20, remove portA from VLAN 10 and add to VLAN 20.
step 2 - Send broadcast packets tagged for each VLAN in the promiscuous port.
step 3 - Check they are only forwarded out the host ports in that VLAN.

test_cases.desc: Multiple isolated vlans with same promiscuous port in both, host port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a second isolated VLAN 20, remove portA from VLAN 10 and add to VLAN 20.
step 2 - Send broadcast packets tagged for each VLAN in the promiscuous port.
step 3 - Check they are only forwarded out the host ports in that VLAN.

test_cases.desc: Mix of isolated and standard VLANs with promiscuous port in both, promiscuous port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a normal access VLAN 20 and add the promiscuous port to it.
step 2 - Remove portA from VLAN 10, set it to access mode and add to VLAN 20.
step 3 - Send tagged broadcast packets from the promiscuous port and check they go only to the tagged VLAN.

test_cases.desc: Mix of isolated and standard VLANs with the same promiscuous port in both, send host & access port packets.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a normal access VLAN 20 and add the promiscuous port to it.
step 2 - Remove portA from VLAN 10, set it to access mode and add to VLAN 20.
step 3 - Send tagged packets from the host/access ports and check they go only to the promiscuous port.

test_cases.desc: Mix of isolated and standard VLANs with promiscuous port in both, promiscuous port packets.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a normal access VLAN 20 and add the promiscuous port to it.
step 2 - Remove portA from VLAN 10, set it to access mode and add to VLAN 20.
step 3 - Send tagged packets from the promiscuous port and check they go only to that VLANs ports.

test_cases.desc: Mix of isolated and standard VLANs with promiscuous port in both, host/access port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a normal access VLAN 20 and add the promiscuous port to it.
step 2 - Remove portA from VLAN 10, set it to access mode and add to VLAN 20.
step 3 - Send tagged broadcast packets from the host/access ports and check they go only to that VLANs ports.

test_cases.desc: Multiple isolated vlans with same promiscuous port in both, bad VLAN tag host port broadcast.
test_cases.method:
step 1 - Set up a second isolated VLAN 20, remove portA from VLAN 10 and add to VLAN 20.
step 2 - Send broadcast packets from the host ports tagged with the other VLANs number.
step 3 - Check all the packets are dropped.

test_cases.desc: RED: GEC-6 - Invalid input validation for interface admin status via SNMP (INTEGER OID)
test_cases.method:
- Verify that INTEGER OID input validation is enforced via SNMP ifAdminStatus
  OID: IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus (1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7.<ifIndex>)
  Only INTEGER values 1 (up) and 2 (down) are valid
1. Configure SNMPv3 user with authPriv access and write permissions
2. Find ifIndex for the test interface (portB) via snmpwalk on IF-MIB::ifDescr
3. For each invalid out-of-range integer (0, 3, 100), attempt snmpset ifAdminStatus = VALUE
4. Verify each invalid integer attempt is rejected with a badValue error
5. For each non-integer string value (test, .), attempt snmpset ifAdminStatus = VALUE
6. Verify each type mismatch attempt is rejected (Value out of range)
7. Verify valid INTEGER values 1 (up) and 2 (down) are each accepted and change interface state

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - HTB CIR bandwidth enforcement
test_cases.method:
1. Configure HTB policy with CIR limit (20% of virtual-link speed)
2. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and traffic-control rule matching custom application
3. Generate UDP packets matching application port and send via tcpreplay at line rate
4. Wait for traffic to complete and check traffic-control counters
5. Calculate measured throughput from bytes counted over test duration
6. Verify measured throughput is within 10% of configured CIR
7. Verify traffic was shaped below line rate

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - HTB PIR/CIR bandwidth enforcement validation
test_cases.method:
1. Configure HTB policy with CIR (15% of virtual-link) and PIR (40% of virtual-link) limits
2. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and traffic-control rule matching custom application
3. Generate UDP packets and send via tcpreplay at line rate for 30 seconds
4. Wait for traffic to complete and check traffic-control counters
5. Verify throughput is at or above CIR (traffic shaping active)
6. Verify throughput does not exceed PIR +10% (upper limit enforced)
7. Verify packets were dropped (rate limiting active)

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - WRR weighted bandwidth distribution
test_cases.method:
1. Configure WRR policy with three classes having weights 50:30:20
2. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and rules matching three applications to each class
3. Generate UDP packets for each class and create separate pcap files
4. Send traffic for all three classes simultaneously using parallel threads
5. Wait for traffic to complete and check traffic-control counters
6. Calculate byte distribution percentage across all classes
7. Verify each class received bandwidth within 5% of expected weight
8. Verify weight ordering is correct: HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - Priority strict ordering verification
test_cases.method:
1. Configure Priority policy with three classes at priority levels 15, 10, and 5
2. Constrain total bandwidth to 50Mbit to force prioritization
3. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and rules matching three applications to each class
4. Generate UDP packets for each class and send simultaneously via parallel threads
5. Wait for traffic to complete and check traffic-control counters
6. Verify strict priority ordering: HIGH bytes > MEDIUM bytes > LOW bytes
7. Verify high-priority traffic received at least 40% of total bandwidth
8. Verify high-to-low ratio is at least 1.5:1 (high priority dominance)

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - Priority policy starvation prevention
test_cases.method:
1. Configure Priority policy with HIGH class (priority 15, max 30Mbit) and LOW class (priority 5)
2. Constrain total bandwidth to 100Mbit via virtual-bandwidth setting
3. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and rules matching applications to each priority class
4. Create 500 packets for each priority class
5. Send high-priority and low-priority traffic simultaneously using parallel threads
6. Wait for traffic to complete and check traffic-control counters
7. Verify both priority classes received traffic (starvation prevention working)
8. Log the high-to-low packet ratio

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - Application-based traffic matching and classification
test_cases.method:
1. Configure HTB policy with three application classes (APP1, APP2, APP3) at different CIR rates
2. Configure zones (LAN and WAN) and rules matching each application to its class
3. Create known packet counts: 150 APP1, 200 APP2, 250 APP3, and 100 unmatched packets
4. Send each set of packets sequentially with short delays between
5. Wait for counters to stabilize and check traffic-control counters
6. Verify each class counter matches packets sent within 5% tolerance
7. Verify default class catches unmatched traffic with accurate count
8. Verify total packets counted matches total packets sent

test_cases.desc: Traffic Control - Multi-zone traffic matching
test_cases.method:
1. Create zones: WAN (0.0.0.0/0), LAN_USERS (192.168.10.0/24), LAN_SERVERS (192.168.20.0/24)
2. Configure HTB policy with USER_TRAFFIC (10Mbit) and SERVER_TRAFFIC (50Mbit) classes
3. Configure rules matching application from each LAN zone to its respective class
4. Generate 200 packets from USER zone (src 192.168.10.50) and 200 from SERVER zone (src 192.168.20.50)
5. Send traffic from each zone sequentially
6. Wait for counters to stabilize and check traffic-control counters
7. Verify USER zone traffic classified to USER_TRAFFIC class within 5% tolerance
8. Verify SERVER zone traffic classified to SERVER_TRAFFIC class within 5% tolerance
9. Calculate and verify overall zone classification rate is at least 80%

test_cases.desc: Test checks if vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled creates a unicast MAC arp entry with port always set as Flooding
test_cases.method: Sets up a vlan with arp-mac-disparity unicast and initiate a ping to a destination ip,capture the arp request from DUT and send response with differing src MAC and ARP layer src MACconfirm the arp layer src MAC is learnt as an arp entry with port type set to flood.Also confirm that no entry is created in the mac-address table corresponding to arp layer src MAC

test_cases.desc: Test checks if vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled creates a multicast MAC with port always set as Flooding
test_cases.method: Sets up a vlan with arp-mac-disparity and initiate a ping to a destination ip,capture the arp request from DUT and send response with differing src MAC and ARP layer src MACconfirm the arp layer src MAC is learnt as an arp entry with port type set to flood.Also confirm that no entry is created in the mac-address table corresponding to arp layer src MAC

test_cases.method: An arp entry is created with multiple ports, ping is done for the ip.confirm ICMP echo request is received on the ports

test_cases.method: A unicast mac is learnt on the vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled and ethernet frames with that unicastmac is sent over the vlan, confirm its flooded to other ports in the vlan

test_cases.desc: Test checks if vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled learns a multicast MAC with port set as Flooding and then sends pkts destined to that MAC address
test_cases.method: A multicast mac is learnt on the vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled and ethernet frame with that dst multicast mac is sent over the vlan, confirm its flooded on member ports in the vlan

test_cases.desc: Test checks if vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled learns a multicast MAC with port set as Flooding and then sends pkts destined to that MAC address and confirms it does not flood other vlans
test_cases.method: A multicast mac is learnt on the vlan with arp-mac-disparity enabled and ethernet frame with that dst multicast mac is sent over the vlan, confirm its not sent to different vlans

dutA should learn all MACs

test_cases.desc:
Boot System: Check the Boot System Backup release
 cannot be set to the same as the Boot System release.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System release
2. Set the Boot System Backup release to the same file
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the Boot System current and backup cannot be set to a file name that has now been moved to a different name.
test_cases.method:
1. Move a release file to a new name
2. Set the Boot System current the previous relase file name which is now nonexistent
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the Boot System current and backup release cannot be set to a file that does not have the correct file extension
test_cases.method:
1. Rename a release file to a '.cfg' file
2. Set the Boot System current and then the backup to the '.cfg' file
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the Boot System current and backup relesae cannot be set to a validly named release file that is not a valid release version file.
test_cases.method:
1. Create a simple text file named with a valid release file name extension
2. Set the Boot System current and then backup release to the fake release file
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check both the Boot System current and backup cannot be set to a nonexistent file.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System current and then the backup release to the name of a nonexistent file
2. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the file set as the Boot System current and backup cannot be moved to a different name.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System current and backup to a valid release
2. Move the file set as Boot Sytem current and backup
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the file set as the Boot System current and backup cannot be edited.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System current and backup to a valid release
2. Edit the file set as Boot Sytem current and backup
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the file set as the Boot System current and backup cannot be deleted.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System current and backup to a valid release
2. Delete the file set as Boot Sytem current and backup
3. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot System: Check that the file set as the Boot System current and backup can be copied.
test_cases.method:
1. Set the Boot System current to a valid release
2. Set the Boot System backup to nothing
3. Delete the backup release from flash
6. Clear the boot system current setting and set backup to a valid file name
7. Delete the main releas from flash

test_cases.desc: Bootup process - "Verifying release" is displayed
test_cases.method: 3. Verify the DUT displays 'Verifying release' during the bootup process

test_cases.desc: Bootup process - "Booting..." is displayed
test_cases.method: 3. Verify the DUT displays 'Booting...' during the bootup process

test_cases.desc: SD Card is present
test_cases.method: 1. If DUT shows an SD card slot, fail if there is no SD card

test_cases.desc: USB Media is present
test_cases.method: 1. If DUT shows a USB slot, fail if there is no USB media

test_cases.desc: Skip Default config
test_cases.method:
1. Check default and currrent boot config settings
2. Add config 'log console level alerts' to the current config
3. Enter the Boot menu and select option 5 - Special boot options
4. Select option 1 - Skip startup script (Use system defaults)
5. On reboot check that the default boot config was used by checking that 'log console level alerts' was not configured

test_cases.desc: Filenames named ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel - Flash
test_cases.method:
1. Create copies of the main release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel and store it in flash2. Set the Boot System current to a release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel
3. Set the default Boot Source to flash
4. Check the release file ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel is used to boot from after each reboot

test_cases.desc: Filenames named ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel - SD Card
test_cases.method:
1. Create copies of the main release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel and store it in flash and SD card2. Set the Boot System current to a release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel
3. Set the default Boot Source to flash and to SD card with a reboot in between
4. Check the release file ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel is used to boot from after each reboot

test_cases.desc: Filenames named ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel - USB media
test_cases.method:
1. Create copies of the main release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel and store it in flash and USB media2. Set the Boot System current to a release file called ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel
3. Set the default Boot Source to flash and to USB media with a reboot in between
4. Check the release file ---w-z-03-09-a-y---.rel is used to boot from after each reboot

test_cases.desc: Try release for different platform
test_cases.method:
1. From the Boot Menu, perform a one off TFTP boot using a release intended for a different platform
2. Check an error is reported

test_cases.desc: Boot default off sdcard
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System default current to sd card and backup to flash, then reboot
2. Check Boot System to confirm device has booted from sd card

test_cases.desc: Boot default off usb
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System default current to USB and backup to flash, then reboot
2. Check Boot System to confirm device has booted from USB

test_cases.desc: Boot fails with no release set
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System current and backup
2. Set Boot Menu Default Boot from Boot System current and backup and reboot
3. Delete release file set as Boot System current
4. Check Boot System current is blank  and reboot
5. Check boot fails with appropriate error message

test_cases.desc: Boot with release, same name as cli
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System current and backup
2. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from TFTP and reboot
3. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from flash and reboot
4. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from SD card and reboot
5. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from USB and reboot

test_cases.desc: Boot with release, same name as cli - SD Card
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System current and backup
4. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from SD card and reboot

test_cases.desc: Boot with release, same name as cli - USB Media
test_cases.method:
1. Set Boot System current and backup
2. Set Boot Menu Default Boot to boot from USB and reboot

test_cases.desc: Check bootloader version
test_cases.method:
1. Show system information in Bootloader Menu and check the bootloader version
2. Restart from Bootloader Menu and check bootloader version is seen at boot time

test_cases.desc: Restart from boot menu
test_cases.method: 1. Enter Boot Menu and select option, 0. Restart and check the device boots

test_cases.desc: Boot from backup (b)
test_cases.method:
1. Enter Boot Menu and select option, B. Boot backup software
2. Check that the current release loaded is the backup release

test_cases.desc: Test all options for default boot
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check default boot from flash - will boot to current boot image when set
3. Check default boot from CLI - will boot to backup boot image when current boot image is not set
4. Check default boot from CLI - will boot to current boot image when backup boot image is not set
5. Check default boot from CLI - will fail to boot when both current boot image and backup boot image are not set
6. Check default boot from SD Card - boot using a file from the SD Card, if supported
7. Check default boot from USB - boot using a file from the USB storage device, if supported

test_cases.desc: Test all options for default boot - SD Card
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check default boot from SD Card - boot using a file from the SD Card

test_cases.desc: Test all options for default boot - USB Media
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check default boot from USB - boot using a file from the USB storage device

test_cases.desc: Test all options for one-off boot
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check one-off boot main release filesystem and check default boot reverts to tftp boot
3. Check one-off boot backup release filesystem and check default boot reverts to tftp boot
4. Check one-off boot tftp copy and check default boot reverts to tftp boot

test_cases.desc: Test all options for one-off boot - SD Card
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check one-off boot from SD Card and check default boot reverts to tftp boot, if supported
6. Check one-off boot from USB storage device and check default boot reverts to tftp boot, if supported

test_cases.desc: Test all options for one-off boot - USB Media
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check one-off boot from USB storage device and check default boot reverts to tftp boot, if supported

test_cases.desc: Test all options for one-off boot - YMODEM
test_cases.method:
1. Check menu return to Boot Menu
2. Check one-off boot from YMODEM and check default boot reverts to tftp boot, if supported

test_cases.desc: Test one-off boot can read all of the flash
test_cases.method:
1. Fill flash with release files
2. Check one-off boot lists all release files

test_cases.desc: Test one-off boot can boot from all of the flash
test_cases.method:
1. Fill flash with release files
2. Check one-off boot lists all release files
3. Check one-off boot can boot each of the release files

test_cases.desc: Test setting Boot System to SD Card without a backup
test_cases.method:
1. Unset Boot System and Boot System Backup
2. Set the Boot System current to a release on SD card
3. Check for the correct error message
4. Set the Boot System current to a release on SD card
5. Check for the correct error message

test_cases.desc: Test setting Boot System to USB Media without a backup
test_cases.method:
1. Unset Boot System and Boot System Backup
2. Set the Boot System current to a release on USB
3. Check for the correct error message
4. Set the Boot System current to a release on USB
5. Check for the correct error message

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option '0. Restart'
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Check option '0. Restart' reboots the device

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option '1. Full RAM test'
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Run the full RAM test, Option 1.
3. Check 5 iterations of the RAM test are run
4. Check there are no errors reported

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option '2. Quick RAM test'
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Run the quick RAM test, Option 2.
3. Check the RAM test has passed

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option 3, Battery backed RAM (NVS) test
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Run the Battery backed RAM (NVS) test, Option 3.
3. Check the NVS test has run 10 iterations and passed
4. Check there are no errors reported

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option 4, Bootloader ROM checksum test
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Run the Bootloader ROM checksum test, Option 4.
3. Check the checksums have been seen

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option 7, Enter the Bootup stage 2 diagnostics menu
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Enter the Bootup stage 2 diagnostics menu, Option 7.
3. Check the Bootup stage 2 diagnostics menu is displayed

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option 8, Quit to U-Boot shell
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Enter the U-Boot shell, Option 8.
3. Check the system is currently in the U-Boot shell
4. Reset and reboot

test_cases.desc: Diagnostics menu option 9, Quit the menu and continue rebooting
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Diagnostics menu
2. Quit the menu and continue rebooting, Option 9.

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 0, Restart
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu
2. Quit the menu restart the device, Option 0.

test_cases.method: Diagnostics menu option 22

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 4. Erase FLASH (Filesystem only)
test_cases.method: Diagnostics menu option 24

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 5. Card slot test
test_cases.method:
1. Check the SD card slot is supported
2. Enter the Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu
3. Run the card slot test
4. Check the responses as all good

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 7. USB slot test
test_cases.method:
1. Check the USB slot is supported
2. Enter the Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu
3. Run the USB slot test
4. Check USB is initialised and device info has been read

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 8. Quit to U-Boot shell
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu
2. Enter the U-Boot shell - option 8
3. Check that the system is in the U-Boot shell
4. Reset out of the U-Boot shell and go back to AWP

test_cases.desc: Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu, option 9. Quit and continue booting
test_cases.method:
1. Enter the Boot stage 2 Diagnostics menu
2. Select 'Quit and continue booting' - Option 9

test_cases.desc: Access U-boot
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and issue a Ctrl-u to enter Uboot
2. Check Uboot has been accessed

test_cases.desc: Change date in U-boot
test_cases.method:
1. Enter Uboot from Boot Menu
2. Check 'date reset' command works
3. Check 'date' command allows a new date and time to be set

test_cases.desc: Access Security Settings Menu
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Select the option 'S' for 'S. Security Level'
3. Check Security Settings Menu is accessed
4. Select the option '0' for '0. Return to previous menu'
3. Check returned to Boot Menu

test_cases.desc: Set Security Level 2
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Select the option 'S' for 'S. Security Level'
3. Select option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)' and abort setting
4. Select option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)' and input mismated passwords
5. Select option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)' and set password
6. Select option '3. Change Password' and reset the password
7. Select Boot Menu option '1. Perform one-off boot from alternate source' and input incorrect password
8. Select Boot Menu option '1. Perform one-off boot from alternate source' and input correct password
9. Select Boot Menu option '2. Change the default boot source (for advanced users)' and input incorrect password
10. Select Boot Menu option '2. Change the default boot source (for advanced users)' and input correct password
11. Select Boot Menu option '3. Update Bootloader' and input incorrect password
12. Select Boot Menu option '3. Update Bootloader' and input correct password
13. Select Boot Menu option '5. Special boot options' and input incorrect password
14. Select Boot Menu option '5. Special boot options' and input correct password
15. Select Boot Menu option '4. Adjust the console baud rate' and check no password is required
16. Select Boot Menu option '6. System information' and check no password is required
17. Select Boot Menu option '7. Restore Bootloader factory settings' and check no password is required
18. Select Boot Menu option '7. Restore Bootloader factory settings' and check that a restore does not clear the security settings
19. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Set Security Level 3
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Select the option 'S' for 'S. Security Level'
3. Select option '2. Set security Level to 3 (Locked Down)' and abort setting
4. Select option '2. Set security Level to 3 (Locked Down)' and input mismated passwords
5. Select option '2. Set security Level to 3 (Locked Down)' and set password
6. Select option '3. Change Password' and reset the password
7. Select Boot Menu option '1. Perform one-off boot from alternate source' and input incorrect password
8. Select Boot Menu option '1. Perform one-off boot from alternate source' and input correct password
9. Select Boot Menu option '2. Change the default boot source (for advanced users)' and input incorrect password
10. Select Boot Menu option '2. Change the default boot source (for advanced users)' and input correct password
11. Select Boot Menu option '3. Update Bootloader' and input incorrect password
12. Select Boot Menu option '3. Update Bootloader' and input correct password
13. Select Boot Menu option '5. Special boot options' and input incorrect password
14. Select Boot Menu option '5. Special boot options' and input correct password
15. Select Boot Menu option '4. Adjust the console baud rate' and check no password is required
16. Select Boot Menu option '6. System information' and check no password is required
17. Select Boot Menu option '7. Restore Bootloader factory settings' and check no password is required
18. Select Boot Menu option '7. Restore Bootloader factory settings' and check that a restore does not clear the security settings
19. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Check the password length limits, >5 and <24
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Select the option 'S' for 'S. Security Level'
3. Select option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)' and set password to valid max length
4. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
5. Reset the password with a passowrd too long - over 23 characters
6. Reset the password with a valid min length passowrd
7. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
8. Reset the password with a passowrd too short - under 6 characters
9. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Check all the valid characters for use in a password
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Select the option 'S' for 'S. Security Level'
3. Select option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)' and set a valid password with uppercase characters
4. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
5. Reset the password and set a valid password with lower characters
6. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
7. Reset the password and set a valid password with numberic characters
8. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
9. Reset the password and set a valid password that includes spece characters
10. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
11. Reset the password and set a valid password with special characters characters
12. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
13. Reset the password and set a valid password with a combination of all valid characters
14. Check all Boot Menu options for security passowrd requirement
15. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Check that the security level is displayed in the Show Boot output
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Check that security level is displayed correctly in Show Boot when set to 1 (none)
3. Set security menu option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)'
4. Check that security level is displayed correctly in Show Boot when set to 2 (Password Protected)
5. Set security menu option '2. Set security Level to 3 (Locked Down)'
6. Check that security level is displayed correctly in Show Boot when set to 3 (Locked Down)
7. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Check that the passowrd timeout activates after 60 seconds and reboot the device
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Set security menu option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)'
3. Check that the passowrd functions correctly, including one character every 50 seconds
4. Check that passowed timeout reboots the device when not entry is made for 60 seconds
5. Check that passowed timeout reboots the device when a partial entry is made and no furhter entry for 60 seconds
6. Check that passowed timeout reboots the device when a valid entry is made and no Return for 60 seconds
7. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Check that security levels 2 & 3 stop access to Start-Shell
test_cases.method:
1. Reboot and enter the Boot Menu
2. Set security menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)'
3. Check that Start-Shell can be accessed
4. Set security menu option '1. Set security Level to 2 (Password Protected)'
5. Check that Start-Shell can be accessed
6. Set security menu option '2. Set security Level to 3 (Locked Down)'
7. Check that Start-Shell can not be accessed
8. Security Menu option '1. Set security Level to 1 (None)' and check security level has been reset

test_cases.desc: Basic check that all devices are providing POE
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is provided by default
2. Disable POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
3. Re-enable POE and confirm POE is provided again

test_cases.desc: Check device reporting of POE status
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided
2. Disable switch ports and confirm POE is still provided and reported consumption is non-zero
3. Disable POE and confirm POE is no longer provided and reported consumption drops to zero
4. Re-enable POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported consumption is non-zero
5. Re-enable switch and confirm POE is still provided and reported consumption is non-zero

test_cases.desc: Check POE is supplied for all priority settings
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided and default priority is low
2. Change POE priority to critical
3. Confirm POE is still provided and reported priority is critical
4. Disable POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
5. Re-enable POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported priority is still critical
6. Repeat steps 2-5 for high and low priorities

test_cases.desc: Check POE spare pair of 2-pair POE devices
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided and default priority is low
2. Disable data-pair POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
3. Enable spare-pair POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported priority is still low
4. Change POE priority to critical
5. Confirm POE is still provided and reported priority is critical
6. Disable spare-pair POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
7. Re-enable spare-pair POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported priority is still critical
8. Repeat steps 4-7 for high and low priorities

test_cases.desc: Check POE data pair of 2-pair POE devices
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided and default priority is low
2. Disable data-pair POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
3. Enable data-pair POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported priority is still low
4. Change POE priority to critical
5. Confirm POE is still provided and reported priority is critical
6. Disable data-pair POE and confirm POE is no longer provided
7. Re-enable data-pair POE and confirm POE is provided again and reported priority is still critical
8. Repeat steps 4-7 for high and low priorities

test_cases.desc: Check global disable/enable of POE
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided
2. Disable POE globally and confirm POE is no longer provided and reported consumption drops to zero
3. Re-enable POE globally and confirm POE is provided again and reported consumption is non-zero

test_cases.desc: Check high-availability network power behaviour
test_cases.method:
1. Confirm POE is being provided
2. Reboot the DUT and confirm HANP is disabled by default
3. Confirm POE is being provided again4. Enable HANP
5. Reboot the DUT and confirm power is maintained throughout the reboot
6. Disable HANP
7. Reboot the DUT and confirm power is no longer maintained throughout the reboot
